$comment: Explicit, versioned opt-outs for scripts/breaking_schema_check.py (an ENFORCE, blocking gate). The gate's rule is not 'you may not break the contract' — it is 'you may not break it silently'. A change stays allowed; the silence does not. An entry only grants an opt-out when file, rule, reason, and version are all present, AND reason is real prose explaining WHY the tightening is intentional and reviewed — a bare issue/PR reference, 'TODO', 'see PR', or anything under ~20 chars / a single word is rejected (see reason_rejection()). pointer_prefix is optional and defaults to matching every finding for that rule in that file; add it to scope a narrower, single-field opt-out instead. Entries do not expire — a bound-hardening acknowledgement is a permanent historical fact about that contract, not a lease.

This intentionally expands the governed extension vocabulary so schemas can declare mechanically checked cross-field equality. It is contract mechanics only, and consumers of the closed registry must update for the new property.

Registers the Agent Lifecycle Record Part 1 client-boundary disclosure annotation (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:376-408) in the governed x-* extension vocabulary so agent_lifecycle_record/*.json schemas can carry it, matching the existing x-traigent-invariants precedent immediately above. This file is documentation/governance metadata only -- its own header states it is 'not applied as a JSON Schema validator over other schemas' -- so no real request or response payload is ever validated against x_extensions_meta_schema.json itself; the breaking-check finding is the generic conservative heuristic correctly erring cautious on a bare-named resource file, not evidence of an actual wire-consumer break. agent_id is nullable only in the unidentified branch, with paired-null invariants, because inventing an agent would corrupt provenance; identified rows remain string-valued.

Expand-contract: identity_state is dropped from the top-level required list because the active Backend does not yet emit it on every experiment-group item or provenance row. The enum stays closed to identified/unidentified only; absence is handled by a new, strictly validated legacy branch (string agent_id, string-or-null dataset_id, no run_id), never treated as identified or as a certified explicit-none dataset claim. A follow-up MAJOR revision re-tightens this back to required once the Backend backfills the field everywhere.

Retires the subtractive curation vocabulary at the client boundary (#389). `remove_redundant` is removed from the enum because acting on subtractive advice keyed to an observed signal biases the customer's own measurement and is unrepairable -- excluded items carry zero inclusion probability. Measured on a 70-item confirmation set, top-15-by-observed-discrimination pruning gave -0.202 against a true -0.073 (2.77x); random-15 was unbiased at -0.078. Breaking is the intended effect: a consumer still emitting or matching this member must be reconciled rather than silently accepted. Recorded in the disclosure register; reintroducing a subtractive category needs an owner decision. Scoped by pointer_prefix to the one enum that actually carried the retired member: an entry with no prefix defaults to matching every enum finding in the file forever (find_allow_entry uses startswith on an empty string), which would silently pre-authorize unrelated future enum breaks.

ALR-1106 (Agent Lifecycle Record Part 1, Route 1/2 packet): moves AgentLifecycleRecordRef out of this file's own local `definitions` block into agent_lifecycle_common_schema.json#/definitions/AgentLifecycleRecordRef so Route 1's new agent_lifecycle_agent_revision_register_response_schema.json and this Route 5 response share one definition instead of duplicating it -- the contract's exact-override manifest (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:434-437) always named the common schema as this shape's eventual home; ALR-1105 could only leave it local because no Route 1 response schema existed yet on that branch. Replaces minimum: 0 with exclusiveMinimum: 0 to correctly enforce that objective weights must be strictly positive (>0, not >=0). Zero weight on an objective is meaningless in multi-objective optimization and should be rejected; this change prevents silent validation of invalid weight configurations. The breaking-schema-check tool does not dereference the substitution, reporting it as a constraint removal rather than a tightening, but the wire behavior is tightened as intended.

Documents a sibling key the SDK already sends today and the backend already preserves rather than drops (#1334, _collect_sibling_keys/validate_example_result in TraigentBackend/src/models/workflow_metadata.py) -- the runtime contract already accepts input_id on a per-example measure; ExampleMetrics's additionalProperties: false simply never enumerated it. A hypothetical old STRICT response consumer that pinned the previous ExampleMetrics shape could reject the field, but no such consumer is known to exist for this producer-side field; the acknowledgement exists so the gap is closed loudly rather than silently. additionalProperties stays false: this enumerates reality, it does not loosen the contract.

Adds the optional keyed, one-way, client-computed identity digest sibling that TraigentBackend#2821 and Traigent#2191 (paired PRs) already exchange as a preserved sibling key under #1334 read-back fidelity; TraigentBackend#2821's own PR checklist states no TraigentSchema change is required for the wire behavior to work because unknown siblings already round-trip. This closes the documentation gap only. additionalProperties stays false -- every sibling the client may send is now enumerated, not loosened.

Adds the optional keyed, one-way, client-computed identity digest sibling for the produced output, paired with example_digest above and shipped by the same TraigentBackend#2821 / Traigent#2191 pair under #1334 read-back fidelity. Documentation-only closure of the same gap; additionalProperties stays false.

Adds the optional 0.0/1.0 match-indicator sibling shipped by TraigentBackend#2821 / Traigent#2191 under #1334 read-back fidelity. Its absence (never null, never a default 0.0) is semantically load-bearing -- an example with no usable expected answer omits the key entirely rather than being scored as a mismatch -- so it is declared as an optional enum [0.0, 1.0], not a required or nullable field. Documentation-only closure of an already-accepted sibling; additionalProperties stays false.

Adds the optional 12-char lowercase-hex sibling that tags which client key version example_digest/output_digest were computed under, shipped by Traigent#2191 (commit 7559b983, landed after this PR's initial description) under #1334 read-back fidelity. Present only alongside the two digests it tags; its own absence carries no separate meaning beyond 'no keyed digests were produced for this row' (e.g. no project API key configured). Documentation-only closure of an already-accepted sibling; additionalProperties stays false.

Removes the old circularity-prone conditional that made issuer signed_payload claim the client signature was inside the issuer preimage. The v0 correction fixes the signing order: issuer signs the manifest first, then the client signs the complete issuer-signed certificate projection with only the outer co_attestation removed. This is an intentional pre-issuance Certified Agent v0 correction reviewed under ChangeSession cs_3e01e0344f7b19eb, packet pkt_377ce10845456890, with owner approval evt_46090f3116370bd9; the acknowledgement is scoped to this exact schema constraint.

Replaces the two-way signed_payload discriminator with the single issuer-first value [unsigned_manifest]. A client co-attestation is subsequent and signs the complete issuer-signed certificate projection, so it cannot be part of the issuer payload without circularity. measures and metadata.measures were a bare $ref to the flat MeasureResults dict, which only ever described HALF of what the backend's _validate_submission_measures dispatcher actually accepts -- it also routes a list of per-example ExampleMetrics results (the form carrying input_id/example_digest/output_digest/verified_match/signal_key_id) to validate_measures_list.
